text:
sarah.sales: Quick sync — Acme Health is asking about BYOK/HSM options for a Private deployment. They want: CMK in an HSM, rotation every 90 days, audit attestations, and proof of key custody. Need POC steps, latency impact, and pricing options. Can PSE + Security weigh in? cc @mike.pse @devon.security
mike.pse: Thanks — a couple quick clarifying q's: do they want us to integrate with a cloud KMS (AWS KMS / CloudHSM, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or do they plan to physically ship an HSM for on-prem attachment? Also confirm whether they expect Redwood to have any custody of plaintext key material (we should not).
devon.security: On the questionnaire they flagged 'FIPS 140-2 Level 3' and asked for HSM attestation and rotation proof. Short answer: we can support HSM-backed CMKs in Dedicated and Private. Hosted API does NOT support customer-imported keys. We'll need copies of CloudHSM/KeyVault attestation and CloudTrail/audit exports.
andrew.ops: Operational note: every synchronous call to an external KMS will add tail latency. We recommend envelope encryption with short-lived DEKs cached in the runtime to avoid per-request KMS ops. For POC we should define cache TTLs and max QPS to size instances.
mike.pse: Proposed high-level POC flow (to share with customer):

1) Customer creates CMK in chosen KMS (mark as HSM-backed).
2) Customer creates a grant/policy for the Redwood service principal (we'll provide the ARN/identity).
3) At startup, Redwood requests an encrypted data key (GenerateDataKey / WrapKey) and stores the ciphertextBlob. Redwood holds the plaintext DEK only in-memory and caches it for N minutes.
4) During inference we use the DEK to encrypt model artifacts/IVs or to decrypt any workspace secrets; when TTL expires we re-request the DEK.
5) Rotation: customer rotates the CMK; they provide new ciphertextBlob via control plane or we re-run GenerateDataKey and rotate cached DEKs per policy.

Code-ish snippet for the POC doc:
```
// pseudo
resp = kms.GenerateDataKey(KeyId=cmk)
plaintext_dek = resp.Plaintext
ciphertext_blob = resp.CiphertextBlob
// use plaintext_dek in-memory, never persist
cache.set('dek', plaintext_dek, ttl=300)
```

mike.pse: Important to call out to them: Redwood never stores customer CMK private material. We only store ciphertext blobs and ephemeral DEKs in-memory.
sarah.sales: On pricing — the customer asked whether KMS calls are billed separately or included. They expect a line item for KMS usage + HSM attestation support. Thoughts on best way to present pricing?
mike.pse: Recommend two options to propose to the customer:
- Option A (conservative): Dedicated + BYOK: include a per-month Dedicated fee + per-10k KMS call pass-through (we can estimate based on QPS).
- Option B (performance): Dedicated with aggressive DEK caching and pre-warming; amortize KMS cost into Dedicated fee (higher monthly) and cap for overages.
For POC we can waive the KMS pass-through for the first 100k GenerateDataKey calls to make it easier.
devon.security: Also flag legal/product addendum: BYOK means the customer holds responsibility for CMK lifecycle and key compromise notices. We need their security contact to sign the BYOK addendum. We'll also request HSM attestation docs (certificate) and CloudTrail logs for the period of the POC.
andrew.ops: For the latency estimate: if we do a Warm + cached DEK pattern, KMS ops are only at rotation/boot — measured extra latency should be <20ms median for an on-region KMS call but worst-case can be >200ms. We should provide both median and p95 numbers and include region affinity in the runbook.
sarah.sales: Action items:
- Mike (PSE) -> Draft POC runbook + sample IAM/KMS policy and the small config snippet for caching (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Andrew (ops) -> Quick perf estimate table (median/p95 impact) for AWS/GCP, and a recommended default cache TTL.
- Devon (sec) -> BYOK attestation checklist + sample addendum language to attach to SOW.
- Sarah -> Ask Acme for preferred KMS provider and expected QPS, and get security contact.
Everyone ok with that? :thumbsup:
mike.pse: Yep, will start the runbook. I'll attach example IAM grant text and a short checklist for their infra team.
devon.security: I'll draft the attestation checklist and example legal bullet points.
andrew.ops: I'll run a quick test on a small cluster to get real p95 numbers and post results here.
sarah.sales: Great — I'll update Acme and schedule a 30-min technical sync with them for Thursday. Thanks all!
